title: Respect then and now
summary: Young people are freer now and show less respect; more wine is drunk today.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well do people have more or less time for that kind of thing now than they used to?

Well, I don't know what they call, they have better time, and we have what they think, that's what they call. Well they're more freer. They got more joints to go in. And they do more than we did. See? And we respect the public. In my time we respect the public. People don't respect nobody. Not this young generation coming up today. They don't respect nobody. But we did. We wouldn't say a bower in front of a lady of no kind. We respect all of them. White or black, but the people today don't respect nobody. I'll tell you what I think about it though. I think the people of the day drink some more wine than I did when I come along. You very seldom, if a man would drink wine, he'd go in and say, give me a glass of wine. Would they give you a little glass of wine like that? That was it. But today they get a jug of wine. And two people walk up down the street with that jug of wine on their shoulder. But in my days, we had more respect for ourselves than the youngsters got today. See, I can't put us walk up down the street with bottles of beer and bottles of wine. We didn't do nothing like that.
